linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
The week ahead looks quiet for U.S. markets as futures remain flat. Investors are holding their breath for upcoming inflation data and watching the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, where new demands from Iran have dimmed hopes for a quick reopening. This uncertainty is being felt in the UK as well, with warnings that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East could impact economic growth next year by driving up fuel prices and disrupting supply chains.

In the world of AI, OpenAI is making significant moves. Free users of ChatGPT will soon have access to unlimited text chats, removing the rate limits that previously cut off conversations. However, the company is also facing legal and hardware questions. New court filings suggest OpenAI plans to challenge Apple in a trade secrets lawsuit by pointing to Apple's own loose security practices. On the hardware front, reports indicate OpenAI is developing an AI-focused device that functions like a smart speaker, expected to cost between $300 and $400.

Elsewhere in tech and policy, Google Wallet is rolling out a new feature that lets parents set up secure balances for their children, aimed at teaching financial habits with built-in oversight. Meanwhile, in the UK, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced plans to give local councils more power to restrict the number of vape and betting shops, a move intended to help revitalize town centers that have struggled with decline.

Finally, in Washington, President Donald Trump is renewing his attempt to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. This follows a previous effort that was blocked by the Supreme Court, as the administration continues to push for more allies on the central bank's board.

instagram.title: Tech Headlines You Need Today

slides.headline: Tech Headlines You Need Today
slides.subtitle: From new drone taxes to big shifts at OpenAI, here is what is happening in tech.

slides.headline: New tariffs on foreign drones
slides.explanation: President Trump is planning to slap 100 percent tariffs on imported drones and aircraft parts. This move could make buying these devices much more expensive for consumers and businesses alike.

slides.headline: Twitch content feeds AI training
slides.explanation: Amazon is now using user streams from Twitch to train its generative AI models. Many creators are pushing back against the decision to use their content this way.

slides.headline: Google loses another app store battle
slides.explanation: A judge has ordered Google to make it easier for users to install rival app stores on Android devices. This is a major win for developers who want more control over how their apps are distributed.

slides.headline: Microsoft retires the Copilot mascot
slides.explanation: The yellow blob mascot known as Mico is being removed from the Copilot voice mode. Microsoft says the character will move to a different platform where it can be more interactive.

slides.headline: More leadership changes at OpenAI
slides.explanation: Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser is leaving OpenAI after less than a year in the role. Her departure marks the second major executive exit at the company this week.

instagram.caption:
It has been a busy day for the tech industry, from new trade policies to internal shakeups at major AI labs.

instagram.title: Today's Global News in 5 Slides

slides.headline: Today's Global News in 5 Slides
slides.subtitle: From international diplomacy to legal battles, here is what is happening today.

slides.headline: Surveillance in Minnesota
slides.explanation: Federal agents ran an undercover operation targeting progressive groups and unions in Minnesota. This raises important questions about how government agencies monitor political organizations and civil rights.

slides.headline: Texas Legal Battle Over Surrogate
slides.explanation: A California couple and a surrogate are locked in a court dispute in Texas over a newborn with a heart defect. The case highlights the complex legal hurdles families face when navigating surrogacy across state lines.

slides.headline: New Contract for Migrant Kids
slides.explanation: The Trump administration awarded a $150 million contract for migrant children's legal representation to a small Texas firm with ties to the administration. Critics are raising concerns about the process behind this government spending.

slides.headline: Jared Kushner's Middle East Trip
slides.explanation: Jared Kushner is heading to Israel and Egypt next week with Board of Peace officials to discuss the situation in Gaza. His visit marks another attempt at high-level diplomacy in an ongoing regional conflict.

slides.headline: Japan Opposes Russian Island Visit
slides.explanation: Japan's Prime Minister called Vladimir Putin's visit to the disputed Kuril islands absolutely unacceptable. This highlights the ongoing diplomatic friction between the two nations over these territories.
